title: 'Ghost whisperer' fortune teller warns of 'global blackout' and says 'keep cash'
excerpt: Mor Plai previously predicted the 2025 Myanmar earthquake and a plague in Russia, and now she shares her predictions on tech disruptions across the globe as she shares a new stark warning
content:
Mor Plai previously predicted the 2025 Myanmar earthquake and a plague in Russia, and now she shares her predictions on tech disruptions across the globe as she shares a new stark warning

Tiffany Lo Fashion and Beauty journalist, Affiliates

12:53, 23 Nov 2026

A warning about global blackout has gone viral as doomsaying circulated on social media for months, but a string of high-profile outages has now supercharged online warnings. Now a well-known Thai 'ghost whisperer' has shared her predictions for late 2026, hinting that there will be a global blackout and she warned people to keep some cash available.

‌

‌

Mor Plai, who gained attention for her predictions on major world events, predicted the 7.9 magnitude Myanmar earthquake in 2025, and a deadly "pneumonia" in 2026. The predictions left people in awe after reports of a suspected plague-related incident in Russia sparked public concern.

‌

In August, the fortune teller appeared on a YouTube programme to discuss what she claims could happen in the coming months as we approach the end of 2026. She said the world could experience serious communication and technology problems, including widespread internet outages and disruptions affecting telecommunications networks.

Article continues below

Earlier this month, a major global Microsoft outage occurred, leaving millions of users unable to access emails, Teams messaging app or AI assistant. The outage also disrupted NHS England staff but the UK's cyber minister explained it did not affect 999 calls, front line NHS 111 services or cause transport disruption.

Microsoft has apologised and blamed a "technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents" for the problem, saying it was introduced during an "earlier network capacity upgrade".

Mor Plai also mentioned in her predictions that the issue could be systemic rather than limited to one company. She said: "Some mobile phones, communication devices and older software could reportedly become extremely slow or stop working, potentially forcing users to upgrade their equipment."

‌

Mor Plai compared the situation to the likes of the feared Y2K computer crisis and warned that banking systems could also be affected. She suggested people keep some cash on them in case electronic payment systems experience problems.

Over in the US, an avalanche of tech outages affected major banks, companies and government agencies. The outage saw the Federal Aviation Administration ordering a nationwide ground stop on all flights on November 13.

‌

Delta Airlines issued an update later Sunday and apologised to its customers for the delays, with the airline confirming that its automated system for calculating departing flights' weight and balance was back working.

Last Thursday (November 19), a fake warning claiming to be issued by the National Grid about an expected major power outage in the UK has been shared tens of thousands of times on social media.

‌

The unofficial infographic has been shared thousands of times across Facebook and Instagram. It wrote: "A major blackout is expected to affect large parts of the UK on Thursday, 19 November 2026 from 4:00 PM, due to a critical fault in the national grid."

‌

It adds that "power may be lost in homes, businesses, and public services across the UK for an extended period" and encourages people to prepare by keeping a torch handy, charging essential devices and keeping fridge and freezer doors closed.

But A National Grid spokesperson clarified and explained: "We’re aware of a false social media post claiming there will be a National Grid outage on Thursday 19 November 2026.

Article continues below

"There is no outage expected. Please disregard the post and report misinformation to social media platforms. Check our official channels for accurate information."
